name: Connecting Ridge (Shackleton–de Gerlache)
description: Ridge linking Shackleton and de Gerlache craters; among the best-illuminated spots at the pole.

name: Chang'e-7 target (Shackleton rim peak)
description: Candidate landing site on an illuminated peak next to Shackleton crater.
source: CNSA presentation to UN COPUOS, Feb 2025 (88°48'S, 123°24'E; candidate)

name: Malapert Massif
description: Tall massif with good Earth visibility on the near-side-facing flank.

name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
description: Southernmost landing to date, on the Mons Mouton plateau region.

name: Shackleton crater floor (PSR)
description: 4 km-deep crater floor that never sees the Sun.
source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Shackleton (89.67°S, 129.78°E)

name: Haworth crater floor (PSR)
description: Large shadowed crater near Malapert; ice-prospecting target.
source: IAU Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature, Haworth (87.45°S, 4.98°W)

name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
description: Equatorial near-side site: Sun climbs high, ~14.8 days of light then night.

name: Chandrayaan-3 Vikram (Shiv Shakti Point)
description: High southern latitude, but outside the polar terrain model.

name: Chang'e-4 (von Kármán crater, far side)
description: Far side: Earth never rises, so no direct-to-Earth link (it uses the Queqiao relay).
